title: No Hewn Stone Altars
kjv_text: And if thou wilt make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewn stone: for if thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast polluted it.
summary: Stone altars must be of uncut fieldstone; applying a tool pollutes the altar.
immediate_context: Continues the altar law of v.24; Joshua obeys it exactly at Mount Ebal (Josh 8:31).
historical_context: Possibly anti-Canaanite (dressed-stone high places), possibly an iron-taboo (cf. Deut 27:5 'lift up no iron tool'), possibly a theology of the unmanufactured: God's altar must not be human artifice. Solomon's temple, built of elaborately hewn stone, keeps the letter by pre-cutting off-site (1 Kings 6:7) — the Bible's first regulatory workaround.
nt_passages: Mark 14:58 — 'temple made without hands' as the category's afterlife
Acts 7:48 — the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands
usofc_implementation: Enforced literally for the ceremonial Gate Rooms of Covenant courthouses: their altar-tables must be uncut fieldstone, certified tool-free. A niche industry of 'providentially shaped stone' brokers sells suspiciously convenient boulders with notarized no-tool provenance.
constitutional_analogue: None; closest analogue is historic-preservation materials law, weaponized.
scene_ideas: A forensic masonry hearing: microscopy slides projected in court to prove a chisel touched the courthouse altar in 1987, voiding every oath sworn on it since.
The 'convenient boulder' broker showing a client the quarry he definitely doesn't own.
satirical_uses: Off-site fabrication (1 Kings 6:7) is precedent: the whole regime runs on cutting the stone where God isn't looking.
